judged_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-198 — `hubspotRefreshToken` is typed/used as the parsed HubspotToken returned by `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` (accessing `.expiresIn`, `.expiryDate`, `.accessToken` directly), but when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response object instead, so `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined (producing `expiryDate = NaN`) and the unparsed Response object is what gets persisted via `prisma.credential.update` at line 198, corrupting the stored credential key (P2, confidence 65).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the raw `fetch(...)` Response object (no `await response.json()` / parsing). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` the code assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` where the non-sync path returns a `HubspotToken` object from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`, but the sync path will instead return a `Response`. That makes subsequent property access on `hubspotRefreshToken` (e.g., expiry calculations / credential persistence) incorrect at runtime and can lead to invalid/NaN expiry or persisting the wrong structure. This mismatch is directly implied by the diff even though the exact later lines aren’t shown here.
